title: Helm freeze -> rollback mapping and CI skein
content:
Purpose and quick summary:

This working doc captures a pragmatic mapping between Helm value freezes and the concrete rollback steps that CI/CD (GitHub Actions + ArgoCD) will perform for private deployments (VPC / on-prem). It also sketches a lightweight CI "skein" pattern (a small web of jobs) that encodes gating, attestation checks, and an explicit artifact shelving strategy so rollbacks are fast, auditable, and consistent with Terraform module contracts.

Why this exists (problem statement):
- Teams struggle to translate a Helm values freeze (a single boolean/semver knob) into repeatable rollback actions across operator-managed clusters and multi-app ArgoCD trees.
- Current rollbacks are ad-hoc: manual Argo sync, manual image re-tag, and hand-edited Helm values. That creates drift and long outages for Private Deploy customers.
- We need an operator-friendly, minimal-operator-intervention workflow so customers can adopt predictable, auditable rollbacks.

Goals:
- Define a canonical mapping from "helm-value freeze states" to rollback playbook steps.
- Provide concrete CI job sketches that perform promotion, shelving, attestation verification, and rollback.
- Ensure Terraform module compatibility (immutable artifact addresses + inputs that can be reconciled during rollback).
- Automate verification/smoke checks post-rollback and emit telemetry for postmortem.

Scope & assumptions:
- Applies only to private-deployments (VPC and on-prem) managed by our operator and ArgoCD.
- We assume images are signed (cosign) and manifests are generated via our build pipeline (kaniko/kaniko cache).
- Terraform manages cluster-level resources and the operator installs charts; Helm values are stored in git (values.yaml per environment).

Key concepts (terminology):
- Freeze toggle: a Helm value flag or git-locked values.yaml commit that indicates "do not move forward; only run emergency rollback/promote". Example: values.global.release_mode: "freeze"
- Shelved artifact: a promoted artifact (image+manifest bundle) persisted in an artifacts bucket and referenced by an immutable digest tag. Shelved artifacts are the canonical targets for rollbacks.
- Skein: a minimal directed graph of CI jobs that enforce attestation -> promotion -> deploy -> smoke test. The skein allows us to re-run exact steps in reverse for rollback.
- Operator evacuation: small, reversible operator action that detaches traffic (or reduces replicas) to limit blast radius during rollback.

Mapping: freeze state -> concrete rollback steps
- Freeze state: values.global.release_mode = "frozen" (soft freeze)
  - CI: Prevents new auto-promotions; only manual approvals allowed.
  - Rollback action: No automatic rollbacks; create incident runbook and optional staged rollback using 'shelved artifact'.

- Freeze state: values.global.release_mode = "evacuate" (safe-evacuate)
  - CI: Trigger operator evacuation hook (operator API: /v1/evacuate?level=graceful).
  - Rollback action: Reduce replicas to 1 or set traffic to canary-tier, switch feature flags off. Start rollback-to-shelf if health checks fail.

- Freeze state: values.global.release_mode = "rollback_requested" (hard rollback)
  - CI: Immediate checkout of last good release revision (values.yaml and app-of-apps commit) and apply via ArgoCD sync.
  - Rollback action: Operator performs image pin to shelved digest and rotates secrets if needed. Terraform does not change cluster identity; only value/manifest changes are applied.

Checklist: preflight for rollback job
- Ensure last-known-good shelved artifact exists (artifact-bucket/<env>/shelves/REV123) and cosign signature verifies.
- Terraform plan for rollback (only if rollback needs TF-level inputs) must be a no-op for cluster-level resources except possibly variables toggles.
- Owner/approver assigned in incident.
- Run smoke tests locally (k8s port-forward + local healthchecks) — quick pass required.

CI skein sketch (GitHub Actions example, high level):
1) attestation-check (job)
   - inputs: candidate-artifact-digest
   - runs: cosign verify, signature + predicate checks, fetch attestation metadata
   - outputs: attestation-ok=true|false

2) promote-to-shelf (job, needs attestation-ok)
   - publish manifest bundle to artifact-bucket with structured metadata (commit, sha, build-id)
   - tag release mapping file in git: artifacts/ENV/last_promoted -> digest

3) deploy-via-argocd (job)
   - update values.yaml (git commit) to pin image.digest
   - create PR to infra repo or update app-of-apps repo with pinned value
   - ArgoCD app sync triggered automatically (or via API if immediate)

4) post-deploy-smoke (job)
   - run smoke tests; collect latency/health metrics
   - if failure -> trigger rollback job referencing shelf

Rollback job (reverse skein):
- Inputs: target-shelf-digest, incident-id
- Steps:
  a) operator-evacuate at level=soft (reduce load)
  b) update values.yaml to point to target-shelf-digest and commit PR
  c) trigger ArgoCD sync of affected apps (app-of-apps subtree)
  d) run parallel smoke checks; if green, operator-restore traffic; if fail, escalate to manual operator intervention

Terraform notes and module contract reminders:
- Never allow Terraform to compute the promoted artifact digest. Terraform modules must accept an image_digest string variable that is provided by CI at runtime (TF input). The module must treat this as immutable and only for reference in Helm values and k8s manifests.
- Keep a small "deployment-binding" module that maps environment -> artifact-metadata (S3 path, build id, digest). This module's state should be allowed to be updated by CI via a minimal terraform apply with the specific binding only (avoid broad apply on cluster modules).
- Example TF input signature: variable "service_image_digest" { type = string }

Helm values -> rollback mapping examples (operator-aware flags):
- global.image.digest -> pinned digest used by all charts
- operator.taint.on_rollback -> true|false; when true operator will cordon nodes/shift traffic during rollback
- featureX.enabled -> use preflight check to flip during rollback rather than during promotion for safer rollback

Image signing and verification checklist:
- All promoted images must be signed with cosign using KMS-backed keys (customer-managed KMS if private).
- The CI job attestation-check must verify both signature and SLSA-style predicate for provenance.
- Keep a TTL on shelves: 90 days default, extendable for long-lived customers.

Operator evacuation and quick commands (operator CLI examples):
- graceful: rioctl operator evacuate --env=staging --level=graceful --timeout=5m
- hard-evacuate: rioctl operator evacuate --level=hard --force
- restore: rioctl operator restore --env=staging

Telemetry and postmortem hooks:
- CI must emit the following to the release tracing pipeline: build-id, artifact-digest, action (promote|rollback), approver, incident-id, elapsed-time-to-rollback.
- Postmortem template: include artifact shelf path, smoke test logs, ArgoCD sync timestamp, terraform plan diffs, cosign verification output.

Open questions and trade-offs (TODOs):
- Should the promote-to-shelf step also include a small canary deploy to a dedicated canary namespace before shelving? Pros: earlier detection. Cons: doubles build-time and complexity.
- How do we safely allow CI to write minimal TF state in environments that have strict change-control? Propose a micro-apply permission model (CI token restricted to single binding path).
- Decide TTL default for shelves and retention policy for signed images to control storage growth.

Appendix: useful links and quick references
- GH PR template: github.com/redwood-inference/private-deploys/.github/rollout-pr-template.md
- Operator API (internal): https://internal-api.redwood/ops/v1/operator/{evacuate,restore}
- Reference cosign commands: cosign sign --key cloudkms://projects/... ; cosign verify --key ... <image>@<digest>

Notes-to-self (fragments):
- try smaller skeletal skein in staging for two weeks before broad rollout
- coordinate with SRE to ensure argocd app-of-apps can accept quick re-syncs without rate limits
- capture the minimal terraform binding module as a separate repo so we can grant CI narrow IAM
